contribution.position: My reliability position is unchanged. The perf report records p99 of 410ms at peak load against a 250ms budget, about 64% over. The incident log shows two sev2 incidents last quarter, both traced to retry storms. Over-budget latency is the kind of condition that drives client timeouts and retries, so the measurement matches a failure mode already seen in production. The QA turn cites 180ms for p99, but the perf report in the artifact set says 410ms. That conflict has to be resolved before the 'risk is contained' claim can stand. The cost and runbook points are not in dispute, and neither addresses retry-storm exposure. The passing test report (412 passed, 0 failed) does not change this, because functional pass rates say nothing about peak-load behavior. Still needed: (a) whether 410ms comes from the changed code path or the test environment, and the source of the 180ms figure, (b) the client retry and backoff configuration and whether it is bounded at that latency, and (c) a repeat load test with p99 inside budget, or a documented and approved exception.
